meta.title: Mongolian A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Mongolian → English (see the Mongolian, recall the meaning) and English → Mongolian (see an English meaning, recall the Mongolian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no graded Mongolian word list for learners is published under an open licence, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 335 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, people and the family, numbers, time and the days of the week, food and drink, money and shopping, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, animals, school and work, the everyday verbs, and the pronouns, question words and joining words every sentence is built out of — and the other 165 are the commonest remaining words of the Mongolian Wikipedia, counted by the WHOLE word: Mongolian adds its case and tense endings to the word (байшин 'house', байшинд 'in the house', байшингаас 'from the house'; явах 'to go', явна 'goes', явсан 'went'), so those forms are added together. That corpus is encyclopaedic, which shows in the fill (history, government, geography). The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words met most often come first. Only words English Wiktionary has an entry for can be taught here, and some common ones are missing from it (хэцүү 'difficult', эсвэл 'or', хэрэв 'if', буцах 'to return'). Every word is in the Cyrillic alphabet, as Mongolian is written in Mongolia, with no romanisation; the Alphabet deck, first in this collection, teaches the letters. A verb is shown by its dictionary form in -х (явах 'to go'). A noun shows its plural and three of its cases where Wiktionary prints its declension table, and a verb its causative and passive where Wiktionary names them; no form is composed here. Example sentences: 373 of the 500 words have one, from Wiktionary's usage examples and from Tatoeba, which holds about 2,600 Mongolian sentences with a translation; none is invented. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Mongolian voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Mongolian Wikipedia, articles of the 2026-11-01 dump (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
